rationale: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: tv_clip_max 0.05->0.08 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-1: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). iter-1 NUMBERS: SSIM 0.922979, hr 0.132941, PSNR 35.32, RMSE 8.57e-4, elapsed 918s (15.3 of 20 min) -- already the best inference solver on Mayo, cleared baseline. FAILURE MODE: the hard upper clamp f.clamp_(0.0, clip_max) at 0.05 truncates every voxel above mu=0.05, i.e. it caps bone / high-attenuation structures; real Mayo LDCT attenuation exceeds 0.05, so bone detail is flattened. The headroom metric is RMSE-sensitive, so the truncated bone is a direct uncredited RMSE penalty. HYPOTHESIS: raising tv_clip_max 0.05->0.08 lets high-mu bone voxels through, so val_ssim and hr rise above iter-1 (0.923 / 0.133), because the 0.05 clamp was the binding upper constraint on bone and the RMSE-sensitive headroom was penalizing its truncation. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.133 (no gain or regression), the clamp is NOT the binding constraint at this lambda, and iter-3 must instead tune tv_lambda (the data-vs-smoothness balance). BUDGET: tv_clip_max is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- identical iteration count (120) -> identical ~918s wall, ~282s margin under the 1200s 20-min budget preserved. tv_iterations deliberately NOT raised: iter-1 used 918/1200s, so more iters would risk the wall (the failure mode iter-1 flagged). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged.
